# Manuscript analysis / seven beats

| Beat | Original paragraphs | Design treatment |
|---|---|---|
| 1. The lecture | 1 | Teal stage, suited narrator; players / rules / incentives. |
| 2. The status game | 2–3 | Coral tokens for wealth, brand and recognition. |
| 3. Ordinary details | 4 | iPad drawings, room light, Thursday football, Sunday picnic. |
| 4. The question | 5 | Two people and a tablet; “why do you think that?” is the emotional turn. |
| 5. The wrong currency | 6 | Expensive gifts contrasted with attention; retain the bạn xanh joke. |
| 6. The leap to catastrophe | 7–9 | Keep the narrator's rhetoric in the essay; separate evidence notes, no invented demographic chart. |
| 7. The sign-off | 10 | Return to stage; original patriotic/comic closing. |

The tone moves from provocative Vinglish lecture to ordinary intimacy, then exaggerated societal stakes and a comic sign-off. The emotional center is wanting to be known. The interactive artifact asks questions instead of scoring people. The social/film excerpts emphasize curiosity; the unabridged reader and print proof retain the entire argument.

Chapter 08 supplies a neighboring model of dating incentives; Chapter 15 concerns repeated encounters and timing. This chapter shifts the question to what someone values in a relationship. These are editorial comparisons, not invented chronology or later-life commentary by Jason. Neither the original post date nor the author's age is known.
